overall: Atlanta is running warm for mid-June with a high dewpoint of 73.4°F adding to the heat index, but the temperature peaked around 12:50 PM ET at 89.6°F and has since dropped sharply to 78.8°F by 14:30 ET. The steep cooling velocity of -5.4°F/hr and the 10.8°F gap between the current temp and the running max strongly indicate the daily high has already been set.
forecast_obs_notes: GFS, ECMWF, and HRRR are tightly clustered at 89.9–90.3°F, suggesting models anticipated a marginally higher peak than what was observed; NBM at 87.5°F is already well below the running max and has been exceeded. The even ensemble model (Tier 1, 58% confidence) targeting 90–91°F is the only credible bull case for a late-day rebound, but the odd model (Tier 4, 12%) at 87–88°F is already moot.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max plateaued at 89.6°F for nearly two hours and the current temperature falling rapidly at -5.4°F/hr, a rebound to surpass the existing high is very unlikely — it would require an anomalous reversal against the established cooling trend. The NWP models' 89.9–90.3°F targets were close but appear to have slightly overshot; confidence is high that 89.6°F is the final daily maximum, with only a small tail risk of reaching 90°F if an unexpected warm surge occurs in the late afternoon.
